reason: Developing red cells have ribosomes, and the supplied materials can make their oxygen-binding haemoglobin.
expectation: The developing cells will produce haemoglobin and mature toward oxygen-carrying red cells.

effect: The developing cells became mature red blood cells containing assembled haemoglobin, ready for the oxygen-binding construction.
reaction: The cutaway usefully distinguishes haemoglobin production in developing cells from the mature cells without nuclei.
reason: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which should bind the available oxygen.
expectation: Oxygen will bind to haemoglobin in the red blood cells.

alternatives.reason: Making plasma is another clear step toward assembling blood.

effect: Oxygen binding and release are shown as reversible, completing that goal; blood assembly remains.
reaction: The double arrow and explanation make the release in low-oxygen tissues clear.
reason: Plasma solutes dissolved in water should form the fluid component of blood.
expectation: This will make plasma for assembling blood.

effect: Plasma is now available as the fluid component for blood assembly.
reaction: The straw-yellow drop makes the plasma distinct from plain water.
reason: Red blood cells suspended in plasma are a natural next step toward assembling blood.
expectation: The red cells will join the plasma, leaving white cells and platelets to complete the blood.

effect: The partial blood sample now contains plasma and oxygen-bearing red cells; white cells and platelets are still missing.
reaction: The picture clearly identifies what remains to be added.
reason: Adding the white cells and platelets should complete the blood sample.
expectation: The remaining cellular components will join the plasma and red cells, completing blood assembly.

effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood sample and the remaining goal.
reaction: The final picture brings the different components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding oxygen to red cells was most worthwhile: the double arrow and explanation connect reversible haemoglobin binding to oxygen release in tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma and then adding red cells was clear but relatively predictable, with little explanation beyond the pictured components.

surprise.text: The developing-cell cutaway clarified that haemoglobin is assembled before maturation into red cells without nuclei.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the final explanation names white cells and platelets without explaining their functions.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers close to tissues, building on the oxygen-release explanation.
